novel_features.name: Bulk address cleaning
novel_features.description: Clean a CSV of raw addresses into standardised, validated, geocoded rows: up to 3 calls per uncached address (about 16 a day per token); overflow rows are marked deferred.
novel_features.rationale: Composes three endpoints with rate-limit back-off, retries and a resumable local cache that single API calls cannot provide.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when you have more than a handful of addresses to standardise, validate or geocode; cached rows cost nothing on a rerun.

novel_features.name: Trip quote
novel_features.description: Get distance, traffic ETA and toll plazas for a trip in one record. Costs up to 4 calls per lane (geocode from and to, route, toll).
novel_features.rationale: Chains the route polyline into toll-by-polylines and geocodes addresses from cache, which users otherwise stitch by hand.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to cost a lane or answer 'how long and how much toll' without two separate calls.

novel_features.name: Service-area coverage check
novel_features.description: Flag orders that fall outside a hub's 45-minute (or N km) service area. Costs 1 isochrone call plus 1 call per uncached address.
novel_features.rationale: Joins the isochrone polygon, cached geocodes and a local point-in-polygon test.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before dispatch to separate serviceable orders from out-of-area ones.

novel_features.name: Fleet plan from orders file
novel_features.description: Turn an orders file of addresses or coordinates into per-vehicle stop sequences. Costs 1 call per 50 orders from a separate 5-per-day route-plan pool; about 30s each.
novel_features.rationale: Automates geocode prep and the 50-order chunking around route-plan, then merges the results.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an orders sheet exceeds the 50-order route-plan limit or has only addresses.

novel_features.name: Cached-address quality report
novel_features.description: See address quality and granularity broken down by pincode or city across everything you have cleaned. Local-only and free; empty until address clean has run.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates the local cache; the API has no list endpoints to answer this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to find which pincodes produce the worst addresses.

novel_features.name: Duplicate-doorstep finder
novel_features.description: Find repeated delivery locations among addresses you have cleaned. Local-only and free; empty until address clean has run.
novel_features.rationale: Groups cached addresses by standardised text or geocodes within N metres.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to catch duplicate orders to the same doorstep.

narrative.headline: Every Delhivery Maps endpoint, plus quota-aware address cleaning, trip costing and fleet planning that resume after quota or expiry stops a run.
narrative.value_prop: Run any of the 13 Delhivery Maps endpoints (India only) from the terminal, then batch work with 'address clean', cost a lane with 'trip quote', check service areas with 'coverage check' and plan routes from an orders sheet with 'fleet plan'. The gateway allows about 50 requests per 24 hours per token (route-plan has its own pool of 5), so the batch commands count their own calls, cache results, and mark work they cannot afford as deferred rather than failing.
narrative.auth_narrative: Delhivery Maps uses a Bearer JWT. The docs site issues a 24-hour web-session token after phone-OTP login (the CLI does not refresh it; when calls start failing with exit code 4, set a fresh one); commercial keys are issued under an enterprise agreement. Set DELHIVERY_MAPS_TOKEN or run 'auth set-token'; 'auth status' reads the token's expiry locally without printing it and costs no quota, whereas 'doctor' makes a live request.

quickstart.command: delhivery-maps-pp-cli which "toll cost for a truck lane"
quickstart.comment: Confirm the install and find the right command; runs offline, no quota spent

quickstart.command: delhivery-maps-pp-cli geocode --address "flat 4b, lotus apt, sec 45, gurgaon, haryana 122003"
quickstart.comment: Smallest real call: address to coordinates (spends 1 of your ~50 daily quota calls)
Reverse geocode a coordinate to a structured address (1 quota call)
Route plus toll plus ETA in one record (up to 4 quota calls: two geocodes, route, toll)

troubleshoots.fix: The 24h web-session token expired; run 'delhivery-maps-pp-cli auth status' then set a fresh DELHIVERY_MAPS_TOKEN

The gateway allows about 50 requests per 24 hours per token, and fleet plan (route-plan) has a separate pool of about 5 per 24 hours. A 429 makes the batch commands lock out that pool for 24 hours (override with DELHIVERY_MAPS_IGNORE_LOCKOUT=1) and defer the rest of the run with exit 0 and rate_limited:true; fully cached items are still served. Rerun after the window with --resume (address clean) so cached rows cost no calls

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for India-only geocoding, address validation and standardisation, driving routes with tolls, distance matrices, reachability polygons and delivery route planning. Pick it over a raw API client when a job involves many rows, needs resumability, or chains route and toll.

recipes.title: Clean an order file
recipes.explanation: Standardises, validates and geocodes every row, caching results so a rerun skips finished rows.

recipes.title: Cost a truck lane, narrowed output
recipes.command: delhivery-maps-pp-cli trip quote --from "Sector 45 Gurgaon" --to "Jaipur" --vehicle bus_truck --agent --select distance_km,total_toll_inr
recipes.explanation: Returns only distance and total toll.

recipes.explanation: Returns a decoded GeoJSON polygon ready for geojson.io or QGIS.
